pr.title: Anonymous: Add configurable device limit

raw_findings.body: tagDeviceUI (impl.go) calls a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...) before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so the failed device's cache key is already set; on retry tagDeviceUI hits the cache and returns nil, TagDevice succeeds, and Authenticate grants anonymous access even though the device was never stored — the configured device limit is trivially bypassed and the device is not counted
raw_findings.evidence:
if errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) {
			return nil, err
raw_findings.failure_mode: Enforcement of the new device limit only works on the first request per device per cache TTL; any retry defeats the limit
raw_findings.impact: tagDeviceUI (impl.go) calls a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...) before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so the failed device's cache key is already set; on retry tagDeviceUI hits the cache and returns nil, TagDevice succeeds, and Authenticate grants anonymous access even though the device was never stored — the configured device limit is trivially bypassed and the device is not counted
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch makes TagDevice errors authoritative for authentication while leaving the pre-existing cache-populate-before-store ordering in tagDeviceUI, which now caches devices that were rejected by the store
raw_findings.suggested_fix: In tagDeviceUI, only set the localCache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (or remove the cache key when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached)
raw_findings.title: Device limit can be bypassed by retrying: localCache is populated before the store rejects the device
raw_findings.trigger: device_limit is configured and reached; a new anonymous device sends a request (denied with ErrDeviceLimitReached), then simply retries the request within the 29-minute localCache TTL

raw_findings.body: Wire generation fails (missing int64 provider / unused provider), or the stale checked-in wire_gen.go still calls ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore) and passes the store into the old ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature, causing a compile error
raw_findings.failure_mode: Build/codegen failure of the server binary until wire configuration is reconciled
raw_findings.impact: Wire generation fails (missing int64 provider / unused provider), or the stale checked-in wire_gen.go still calls ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore) and passes the store into the old ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature, causing a compile error
raw_findings.root_cause: Constructor signature and injection topology changed without updating the wire provider set that references the old signature
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and the `wire.Bind(new(anonstore.AnonStore), new(*anonstore.AnonDBStore))` entries from pkg/server/wire.go and regenerate wire_gen.go, since the store is now constructed inside ProvideAnonymousDeviceService
raw_findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature changed but wire.go still registers it, breaking dependency-injection generation/build
raw_findings.trigger: Running `wire` generation or building the server: pkg/server/wire.go:374 still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds AnonStore to *AnonDBStore, but the constructor now requires an `int64` for which no wire provider exists, and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer consumes AnonStore

raw_findings.body: All concurrent requests pass the count check and insert new rows, so the number of stored anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit
raw_findings.failure_mode: Configured limit is a soft bound that can be overshot under concurrent load
raw_findings.impact: All concurrent requests pass the count check and insert new rows, so the number of stored anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit
raw_findings.root_cause: The limit check (CountDevices) and the insert are separate, non-serialized statements with no transactional guard
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce the limit atomically, e.g. perform the count and insert in a single transaction with appropriate locking, or use a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE count < limit
raw_findings.title: TOCTOU race between CountDevices and insert allows exceeding the configured device limit
raw_findings.trigger: Multiple new anonymous devices authenticate concurrently (or across multiple Grafana instances) while the device count is just below the limit; each request reads count < deviceLimit before any of them inserts

raw_findings.body: A legitimately registered device within the limit receives ErrDeviceLimitReached and is denied anonymous access
raw_findings.failure_mode: Spurious authentication denial for existing devices on MySQL
raw_findings.impact: A legitimately registered device within the limit receives ErrDeviceLimitReached and is denied anonymous access
raw_findings.root_cause: RowsAffected == 0 is treated as 'device does not exist' but on MySQL it also means 'row matched but values unchanged'
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish 'row not found' from 'row unchanged', e.g. by first selecting the device or by enabling clientFoundRows semantics / checking existence explicitly instead of relying on RowsAffected
raw_findings.title: updateDevice misreports ErrDeviceLimitReached when MySQL returns 0 affected rows for an identical-value update
raw_findings.trigger: MySQL backend at the device limit; an already-registered device re-authenticates (e.g. from another HA instance without a warm localCache) with unchanged client_ip/user_agent and an updated_at that rounds to the same second as the stored value — MySQL's RowsAffected is 0 when no column value changes

raw_findings.body: The retried Exec receives the SQL string twice (as statement and as first bind argument), producing a SQL error or wrong bindings, so the device update fails and the request is incorrectly rejected with an error
raw_findings.failure_mode: Intermittent update failures under DB contention where a retry should have succeeded
raw_findings.impact: The retried Exec receives the SQL string twice (as statement and as first bind argument), producing a SQL error or wrong bindings, so the device update fails and the request is incorrectly rejected with an error
raw_findings.root_cause: New closure reassigns the captured slice on each invocation, making the callback non-idempotent under the session retry mechanism
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Build the Exec argument slice in a local variable inside the closure (e.g. `execArgs := append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`) instead of reassigning the captured `args`
raw_findings.title: updateDevice mutates captured args slice inside the session closure, corrupting the query on retry
raw_findings.trigger: WithDbSession retries the callback (e.g. SQLite 'database is locked' retry logic); on the second invocation the outer `args` slice already has the query prepended, so the query string is prepended a second time

raw_findings.root_cause: Initializer-only declaration without a type annotation narrows the inferred property type to `undefined`
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the field explicitly: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (or `= 0` to match the backend's non-optional int64 serialization)
raw_findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit class field lacks a type annotation, so its type is inferred as `undefined`
raw_findings.trigger: Any TypeScript consumer reads `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` from GrafanaBootConfig and tries to use it as a number

On retry within TTL, tagDeviceUI returns nil at L84, TagDevice succeeds, and Authenticate grants access despite the device never being stored. This is a real logic bug introduced by making TagDevice errors authoritative.

validated_findings.body: Wire generation fails (missing int64 provider / unused provider), or the stale checked-in wire_gen.go still calls ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore) and passes the store into the old ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature, causing a compile error
validated_findings.failure_mode: Build/codegen failure of the server binary until wire configuration is reconciled
validated_findings.impact: Wire generation fails (missing int64 provider / unused provider), or the stale checked-in wire_gen.go still calls ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore) and passes the store into the old ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature, causing a compile error
validated_findings.root_cause: Constructor signature and injection topology changed without updating the wire provider set that references the old signature
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Remove `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and the `wire.Bind(new(anonstore.AnonStore), new(*anonstore.AnonDBStore))` entries from pkg/server/wire.go and regenerate wire_gen.go, since the store is now constructed inside ProvideAnonymousDeviceService
validated_findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature changed but wire.go still registers it, breaking dependency-injection generation/build
validated_findings.trigger: Running `wire` generation or building the server: pkg/server/wire.go:374 still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds AnonStore to *AnonDBStore, but the constructor now requires an `int64` for which no wire provider exists, and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer consumes AnonStore
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The literal search shows pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:43 calls ProvideAnonDBStore directly with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit, bypassing wire injection. The wire.go entry at L374 is unused for this service. No build failure occurs because the store is constructed inline in ProvideAnonymousDeviceService.

validated_findings.body: All concurrent requests pass the count check and insert new rows, so the number of stored anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit
validated_findings.failure_mode: Configured limit is a soft bound that can be overshot under concurrent load
validated_findings.impact: All concurrent requests pass the count check and insert new rows, so the number of stored anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit
validated_findings.root_cause: The limit check (CountDevices) and the insert are separate, non-serialized statements with no transactional guard
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce the limit atomically, e.g. perform the count and insert in a single transaction with appropriate locking, or use a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE count < limit
validated_findings.title: TOCTOU race between CountDevices and insert allows exceeding the configured device limit
validated_findings.trigger: Multiple new anonymous devices authenticate concurrently (or across multiple Grafana instances) while the device count is just below the limit; each request reads count < deviceLimit before any of them inserts
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at L110-115 shows CountDevices and updateDevice/insert are separate non-transactional operations. Multiple concurrent requests can each read count < deviceLimit before any insert, allowing the limit to be exceeded. This is a real TOCTOU race introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: A legitimately registered device within the limit receives ErrDeviceLimitReached and is denied anonymous access
validated_findings.failure_mode: Spurious authentication denial for existing devices on MySQL
validated_findings.impact: A legitimately registered device within the limit receives ErrDeviceLimitReached and is denied anonymous access
validated_findings.root_cause: RowsAffected == 0 is treated as 'device does not exist' but on MySQL it also means 'row matched but values unchanged'
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish 'row not found' from 'row unchanged', e.g. by first selecting the device or by enabling clientFoundRows semantics / checking existence explicitly instead of relying on RowsAffected
validated_findings.title: updateDevice misreports ErrDeviceLimitReached when MySQL returns 0 affected rows for an identical-value update
validated_findings.trigger: MySQL backend at the device limit; an already-registered device re-authenticates (e.g. from another HA instance without a warm localCache) with unchanged client_ip/user_agent and an updated_at that rounds to the same second as the stored value — MySQL's RowsAffected is 0 when no column value changes
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at L95-96 returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected==0. On MySQL, an UPDATE that matches a row but changes no values returns 0 affected rows. An existing device with unchanged client_ip/user_agent/updated_at would be incorrectly rejected. This is a real edge case bug.

validated_findings.body: The retried Exec receives the SQL string twice (as statement and as first bind argument), producing a SQL error or wrong bindings, so the device update fails and the request is incorrectly rejected with an error
validated_findings.failure_mode: Intermittent update failures under DB contention where a retry should have succeeded
validated_findings.impact: The retried Exec receives the SQL string twice (as statement and as first bind argument), producing a SQL error or wrong bindings, so the device update fails and the request is incorrectly rejected with an error
validated_findings.root_cause: New closure reassigns the captured slice on each invocation, making the callback non-idempotent under the session retry mechanism
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Build the Exec argument slice in a local variable inside the closure (e.g. `execArgs := append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`) instead of reassigning the captured `args`
validated_findings.title: updateDevice mutates captured args slice inside the session closure, corrupting the query on retry
validated_findings.trigger: WithDbSession retries the callback (e.g. SQLite 'database is locked' retry logic); on the second invocation the outer `args` slice already has the query prepended, so the query string is prepended a second time
validated_findings.verifier_reason: At L84, args is reassigned inside the closure: args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...). If WithDbSession retries the callback, the outer args slice already has query prepended, causing query to be prepended again. This corrupts the Exec call on retry. The patch introduces this non-idempotent closure.

validated_findings.body: The field's inferred type is `undefined` (not `number | undefined` as declared in GrafanaConfig), so numeric comparisons or arithmetic on the value fail type-checking even though the backend always serializes an int64 into it at runtime
validated_findings.failure_mode: Frontend code consuming the new setting cannot type-check against the intended numeric type
validated_findings.impact: The field's inferred type is `undefined` (not `number | undefined` as declared in GrafanaConfig), so numeric comparisons or arithmetic on the value fail type-checking even though the backend always serializes an int64 into it at runtime
validated_findings.root_cause: Initializer-only declaration without a type annotation narrows the inferred property type to `undefined`
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the field explicitly: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (or `= 0` to match the backend's non-optional int64 serialization)
validated_findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit class field lacks a type annotation, so its type is inferred as `undefined`
validated_findings.trigger: Any TypeScript consumer reads `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` from GrafanaBootConfig and tries to use it as a number
validated_findings.verifier_reason: TypeScript class field inference: the GrafanaConfig interface at packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200 declares anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined. The class implements this interface, so the field type is constrained by the interface, not just the initializer. No type error occurs.

validated_findings.body: The new `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` option is invisible and undiscoverable; Grafana convention requires every ini option to be listed in conf/defaults.ini, and repository search shows no `device_limit` entry in conf/
validated_findings.failure_mode: Undocumented, undiscoverable configuration option shipped to users
validated_findings.impact: The new `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` option is invisible and undiscoverable; Grafana convention requires every ini option to be listed in conf/defaults.ini, and repository search shows no `device_limit` entry in conf/
validated_findings.root_cause: Configuration key was added to the settings reader without the mandatory defaults/sample/docs entries
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `device_limit =` under `[auth.anonymous]` in conf/defaults.ini and conf/sample.ini and document it in docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana
validated_findings.title: New device_limit setting is not documented in conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or configuration docs
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator looks for anonymous-access options in conf/defaults.ini / sample.ini or the configure-grafana docs after this patch merges
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The literal search shows conf/defaults.ini:581 and conf/sample.ini:570 have [auth.anonymous] sections. The claim that device_limit is undocumented is a documentation gap, not a code defect. The patch correctly reads the setting; missing docs is outside code review scope.

validated_findings.body: A regression in updateDevice (e.g. wrong WHERE window or placeholder handling) that rejects legitimate existing devices at the limit would pass the test suite undetected
validated_findings.failure_mode: Untested success path of the new limit feature
validated_findings.impact: A regression in updateDevice (e.g. wrong WHERE window or placeholder handling) that rejects legitimate existing devices at the limit would pass the test suite undetected
validated_findings.root_cause: New enforcement logic has two branches but the test only asserts the rejection branch
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Extend TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit to call CreateOrUpdateDevice again for the first (existing) device while at the limit and require.NoError plus verify updated_at/client_ip changed
validated_findings.title: No test covering the allowed path when the limit is reached: updating an existing device must still succeed
validated_findings.trigger: The only limit test asserts rejection of a new device; the intended 'if device limit is reached, only update devices' branch where updateDevice succeeds for an existing, in-window device is never exercised
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap observation, not a code defect. The test at L51-69 tests rejection; suggesting additional test cases is a style/coverage concern, not a bug introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: The device-limit count window, the admin device-list window, and the usage-stats window would silently diverge, making the enforced limit inconsistent with what admins and stats report
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability defect: semantically coupled windows defined independently in three files
validated_findings.impact: The device-limit count window, the admin device-list window, and the usage-stats window would silently diverge, making the enforced limit inconsistent with what admins and stats report
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces a new copy of the 30-day constant in anonstore instead of consolidating the existing thirtyDays constants
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Export a single shared constant (e.g. anonstore.AnonymousDeviceExpiration) and use it from api/api.go and impl.go instead of three independent 30-day constants
validated_findings.title: 30-day expiration constant now duplicated in three places, risking drift between limit accounting and API listing
validated_findings.trigger: A future change adjusts the device-activity window in one file (anonstore/database.go, anonimpl/api/api.go's anonymousDeviceExpiration, or anonimpl/impl.go's thirtyDays) without the others
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The 30-day constant duplication is a maintainability/style concern, not a functional defect. The patch introduces one new constant; the existing constants in api/api.go and impl.go are pre-existing. No concrete bug is demonstrated.
